supports.where: The sheet's title, before the words Safety Data Sheet: it names no strength, and the supplier lists no other sheet for a solution of ammonium nitrate. Whether it covers the solution on the bench is read from its table of composition, in a row below. The sheet prints no signal word: it has no line that begins Signal Word. Under the heading of section 2 it lists no hazard class, no hazard statement and no code, and has two sentences in their place: that the chemical is taken to be non-hazardous under the GHS classifications of a standard it names, with every laboratory chemical still to be treated with caution, and that reactions nobody foresaw can always happen, so careful practice is to be kept. The note says that the sheet prints neither a signal word nor a statement, and gives the first of those sentences in its own words without naming the standard.
Under the title, after the words Revision Date, and again at the foot of the sheet: the revision that was read.

Section 3, the concentration column, in the row for ammonium nitrate, formula weight 80.04; the rest is water. The sheet does not say on what basis the percentage is. 0.5 mol/L is 40 g in a litre: 4 g in each 100 mL, and a shade under 4% by mass. The note takes the solution on the bench to be at the foot of this range and the sheet to cover it; a solution a little under the range is not one the sheet would rate higher.
The heading of section 8. Under it the sheet calls for eye protection, gloves and protective clothing, and for washing the hands after handling; it prints no code beside either.

The heading of section 4. Under it, for the eyes: they are rinsed with water for several minutes, contact lenses are taken out if they are worn and come out easily, and the rinsing is kept up after that; the sheet prints no code beside this and gives no number of minutes. For the skin: it is washed with plenty of water. Neither is followed by a line on medical advice.
The heading of section 10. Under it the sheet names four kinds of substance the solution is to be kept from; the note gives them in another order and in its own words.
